subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced in the party's conversation as the source of ambient citations that have become a weather condition of their shared experience.
source_quote: I heard Grygum's name pulled into the discussion — Grygum, not me, which is how I know the sentence was reconstructed after the fact

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin responded immediately and mercilessly to the demand for prayer beads, declaring, 'You don't get a question. You did not donate a book.'
source_quote: Thorin's response was immediate and merciless. "You don't get a question. You did not donate a book."

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer was directed to someone named Philemon alongside Thorin, and the speaker later said, 'I'm all up for couples counseling with Dawnbringer.'
source_quote: Thorin and Dawnbringer got directed to someone named Philemon — ... "I'm all up for couples counseling with Dawnbringer."

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a half-elf with a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts, who had previously pursued a quiet, small area of study until a living half-orc cleric walked through his door.
source_quote: His name was Vareth. He had, he explained breathlessly, a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts. Which had, until recently, been a quiet, small area of study.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth grabbed the speaker's hand and dragged them, expressing eagerness to test theories and share knowledge after learning of the speaker's status as a cleric of Bahamut.
source_quote: He grabbed my hand and practically dragged me. ... "And I do have something I can share with you?"

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth recognized and embraced the term 'Stroud's Gambit' as a novel and transformative concept for his field of Bahamut half-orc conversions.
source_quote: "Stroud's Gambit." Vareth stopped. His expression went through several stages very quickly — surprise, recognition, something that looked almost like delight at receiving a gift he hadn't known he wanted. "*Oh.* Oh! Well, that's not how — this is all novel news! I can't wait to take advantage of it!"

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud, a dwarf who couldn't actually play chess, defeated Protanther — an ancient gold dragon who had analyzed the same chess position for four hundred years — by rolling a move that landed perfectly and definitively.
source_quote: A dwarf who couldn't actually play chess, sitting across from an ancient gold dragon who had been analyzing the same position for four hundred years. Protanther had mapped every possible move. He was certain. And then Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly. Definitively.

subject: Protanther
fact: Protanther, an ancient gold dragon, had mapped every possible move in a single chess position for four hundred years and was so stunned by Stroud's move that he joined the alliance.
source_quote: Protanther had mapped every possible move. He was certain. And then Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly. Definitively. Protanther was so stunned he joined the alliance.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the location where scholars are assigned threads, where the First Reader directs academic focus, and where Vareth arrived to confront the First Reader about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.
source_quote: The First Reader assigned scholars. Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — ... The First Reader clarified: not about the party generally, but about *me* in particular. ... came through the door ... directed his outrage squarely at the First Reader

subject: Stroud's Gambit
fact: Stroud's Gambit is the term coined by the speaker to describe the legendary chess move that restructured Vareth's entire academic field and became a catalyst for theological controversy.
source_quote: And then, because I couldn't help it, and because the phrase had been sitting in the back of my mind since we started this journey and I'd never had the right audience for it: "Stroud's Gambit."

subject: Bahamut Half-Orc Conversion Surge
fact: The sudden appearance of a living half-orc cleric of Bahamut triggered a surge of scholarly interest, funding, and conference invitations for Vareth, transforming his quiet niche into a flood of academic activity.
source_quote: The controversy had erupted throughout the realms — what did the sudden half-orc interest in Bahamut mean for the orc pantheon? ... Funding was arriving. A living half-orc cleric of Bahamut had walked through his door.

subject: prayer book
fact: The speaker possesses a prayer book as part of their accumulated notes from months in the Underdark, used to seek answers about Bahamut's intentions and theological landscape.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark

subject: theological documents
fact: Theological documents are among the speaker's accumulated notes from months in the Underdark, used to seek answers about Bahamut's intentions and theological landscape.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark

subject: library
fact: The library within Candlekeep holds answers waiting about Bahamut's intentions, the speaker's conversion, and why Vareth's field became a flood.
source_quote: Somewhere in the library, there were answers waiting. About Bahamut's intentions, about what my conversion meant in the broader theological landscape, about why Vareth's previously obscure field had become a flood.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was assigned the Jimjar thread by the First Reader, which dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific.
source_quote: Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — which apparently dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is known for citing Malfire at every available opportunity, a habit that has become an ambient weather condition for the party.
source_quote: Somewhere in the background, the rest of the party had begun debating Daz's habit of citing Malfire at every available opportunity.

subject: Malfire
fact: Malfire is cited by Daz and referenced by the speaker as an authoritative voice whose words are invoked as definitive truth, particularly in Volume 3.
source_quote: "As Malfire said in Volume 3." Nobody laughed. This was the correct response.

subject: conversion phenomenon
fact: The conversion phenomenon refers to the unexpected emergence of a living half-orc cleric of Bahamut, which triggered theological controversy, academic reorientation, and the birth of the term 'Stroud's Gambit.'
source_quote: The conversion phenomenon that had restructured his entire career. He was trying to find the shape of it, the causality.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is where the assembled scholars are pointed at the speaker like a hospitality service they hadn't paid for, and where the room changed after Vareth's arrival.
source_quote: Looking at the assembled scholars being pointed at us like a hospitality service we hadn't paid for ... And then the room changed.

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker identifies as a cleric of Bahamut who has not yet entered the phase of attempting to take over the world, and who coined the term 'Stroud's Gambit.'
source_quote: "You have to understand... that it is traditional for clerics of Bahamut to want to try to take over the world. But I haven't moved into that phase yet." ... "Stroud's Gambit."

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker takes notes as a consistent practice, driven by curiosity and the need to seek answers about Bahamut's intentions and theological implications.
source_quote: I took notes. It's what I do.

subject: room change
fact: The room changed after Vareth arrived and confronted the First Reader about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut, marking a turning point in the narrative.
source_quote: And then the room changed.

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker says, 'I'm feeling, in demand here,' after Vareth recognizes them as a rare specimen and a living data point.
source_quote: "I'm feeling," I said, to no one in particular, "in demand here."

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker says, 'It's all part of the plan,' in response to Vareth's excitement, adopting a tone of calm authority despite uncertainty.
source_quote: "Oh," I said, as warmly as I could manage, "it's all part of the plan."

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker observes that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks, a belief they find deeply comforting.
source_quote: I had the particular comfort of knowing that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks.
